audit_findings.title: Legacy discontinued operations may consume cash excluded from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed outflows: $40m in 2023, $151m in 2024, $51m in 2025, and $12m in H1 2026; $254m cumulative
audit_findings.mechanism: Legacy cash outflows reduce distributable owner earnings, or require a separate present-value deduction, if they are excluded from continuing-operations OE and the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Cash provided by (used for) operating activities – discontinued operations for the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023 was $(151) million and $(40) million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The cash outflows are demonstrated, but their omission from OE remains conditional on the unreconciled OE construction. The $151m 2024 outflow equals 9.6% of the $1,571.5m anchor OE, and continued outflows through 2026 make the issue reasonably capable of materially lowering the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every OE year to total operating cash flow, identify discontinued-operation amounts already captured, and rerun OE or the bridge using the filed schedule of remaining legacy payments net of qualifying recoveries.

audit_findings.title: Unreserved environmental exposure is absent from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: Latest filed accrual $580m less $363m indemnification asset equals $217m net accrued exposure; adding the $586m possible excess produces a conservative $803m maximum net burden before additional recoveries
audit_findings.mechanism: A net environmental obligation not represented in projected OE would be deducted from the equity bridge; future remediation expense could also reduce OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Therefore, considerable uncertainty exists with respect to environmental remediation and costs, and, under adverse changes in circumstances, it is reasonably possible that the ultimate cost with respect to these particular matters could range up to approximately $600 million above the accrued obligations amount.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge omission is demonstrated for any net obligation not already represented in OE, although the realizable indemnification and timing remain uncertain. A conservative $803m deduction is 3.3% of $24.445bn base equity value, or about $1.19 per share, leaving base value near $35.16 versus the $87.86 price. It therefore does not change the valuation conclusion on the filed range.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $580m accrual and $363m indemnification asset by obligation, establish recoverability and payment timing, and rerun the bridge for the net amount without double counting expenses already included in OE.

audit_findings.title: All cash may not be distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: Up to the full $2.365bn cash and short-term-investment addition; 9.7% of base equity value and $3.52 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Only excess cash belongs in the equity bridge; seasonal working-capital funding, restricted cash and minimum operating liquidity must remain with operations.
audit_findings.evidence: Due to the seasonality of Corteva’s business and the credit programs Corteva may offer its customers, net working capital investment and corresponding debt levels will fluctuate over the course of the year.
audit_findings.explanation: The valuation demonstrably adds the entire June balance, while the filing shows seasonal financing needs, $3.193bn of short-term borrowings, negative $3.345bn first-half continuing operating cash flow and foreign cash used for local operations. The excess portion is unresolved, but the amount at issue is large enough to materially alter the bridge and buy-below price.
audit_findings.action: Calculate normalized cash across the seasonal cycle, identify restricted and locally required balances, determine minimum operating liquidity, and rerun the bridge with only demonstrably excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded benefit cash requirements may differ from the expense retained in OE
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed June 2026 pension and OPEB liability of $1.300bn; $1.460bn discretionary pension contribution comprising $1.061bn paid in June and $399m paid in July; 2025 contributions of $136m versus $36m periodic cost
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash contributions and OPEB claims can exceed the accounting expense embedded in OE, while unfunded obligations or post-balance-sheet funding may require an equity-bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: The company's OPEB plans are unfunded and the cost of the approved claims is paid from operating cash flows.
audit_findings.explanation: The expense-to-cash mismatch is demonstrated, including a major 2026 contribution. The June cash balance already reflects the $1.061bn June payment but not the $399m July payment, and the remaining $1.300bn liability equals 5.3% of base equity value. Allocation in the separation and the portion already represented in OE remain unresolved, but the filed scale is material.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile annual pension and OPEB expense to contributions and claims, update the bridge for the July contribution and remaining net unfunded obligation without double counting, and rerun after the separation documents allocate the plans.

audit_findings.title: EIDP preferred stock creates a numerator-denominator claim test
audit_findings.magnitude: Computed callable claim of $272.16m and annual preferred dividends of approximately $9.98m
audit_findings.mechanism: Preferred dividends must be removed from OE attributable to common stockholders, or the preferred claim must be treated consistently in the equity bridge before dividing by common shares.
audit_findings.evidence: However, EIDP has preferred stock outstanding to third parties which is accounted for as a noncontrolling interest at the Corteva, Inc. level.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed common-stockholder income calculation subtracts $11m-$12m of noncontrolling-interest income in 2023-2025, broadly consistent with the approximately $10m annual preferred dividend, but every OE year still requires confirmation. Even complete omission of the $272.16m callable claim would equal only 1.1% of base equity value, or about $0.40 per common share, and would not alter the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace each OE year to income attributable to Corteva common stockholders, verify the preferred dividends within NCI attribution, and confirm whether redemption is expected before making any bridge adjustment.

audit_findings.title: The stated share ceiling is not a true maximum
audit_findings.magnitude: Conservative computed ceiling of 3.363m additional shares using the entire FY2025 combined RSU-and-PSU pool as PSUs; 0.50% of 672.44m shares and approximately $0.18 per base-value share
audit_findings.mechanism: Maximum PSU settlement increases the fully diluted common-share denominator and lowers value per share.
audit_findings.evidence: The actual award, delivered in Corteva Common Stock, can range from zero percent to 200 percent of the original grant.
audit_findings.explanation: Calling 672.44m a contractual ceiling is demonstrated to be incorrect because PSUs can settle at 200%. However, even the deliberately conservative assumption that every one of the 3.363m combined nonvested RSUs and PSUs receives an additional share changes base value from $36.35 to about $36.17, which is not material to the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the current PSU-only count by grant, apply each grant's maximum payout, reconcile options and separately excluded potential shares to prevent double counting, and update the denominator label and sensitivity.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2019 computed unidentified residual of approximately $998.3m; valuation-period magnitude unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any residual depreciation or amortization proven to be an eligible non-economic charge would be added back to OE, increasing the anchor and operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2019 $599.0m (37.5% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The treatment is conservative rather than an demonstrated overvaluation error. From $599m representing 37.5% of filed FY2019 D&A, the unidentified FY2019 residual computes to about $998.3m, but 2019 is outside the 2020-2024 OE series and the record supplies no corresponding residual amounts or classifications for the valuation years. The possible understatement is therefore unresolved and its materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain filed D&A composition for each 2020-2024 OE year, classify residual items under the owner-earnings rules, and rerun the OE series and trend anchor only for amounts supported as eligible add-backs.
